title: Issa Rae Monologue
text: Ladies and gentlemen, Issa Rae! It's so crazy to be here right now. I cannot believe it. I'm hosting Saturday Night Live, y'all. The stairs, the same stairs as the comedy legends like Tina Fey and Amy Poehler and Molly Shannon. Like, my family, all of our inside jokes are from SNL. This is incredible. And, actually, I'm so scared right now. I'm scared as hell. I'm not gonna lie. I might throw up. But I'm gonna hold it down, because I'm the first black woman to host SNL. Yes! Okay, wait. That's actually not true. Y'all really clapped. Like, okay. What if I just kept lying to y'all all night? Half of y'all wouldn't even notice. But if this show goes bad tonight, just blame it on me. Mary J. Blige. I was actually supposed to host the show back in March when I had two movies and season four of my show, Insecure, coming out. Thank you. But now I'm here, and there really is no reason. Like, I have nothing going on at all. People keep asking me, what have you been working on? And I'm like, uh, puzzles, bitch? I don't know. What have you been working on since you all in my business? But my show premiered exactly four years ago this month. Right before the last election. It was crazy because the results came in, and, of course, everyone was freaking out. I was freaking out, and it just felt really awkward for my life to be going so good, you know? Like, it was rude for me to be peaking right when democracy was collapsing. It's just weird to say, thank God for what happened in the fall of 2016, you know? When I first got a TV show, I thought everything would fit. It feels so different. But it really just felt like high school. You know, the show was kind of based on a web series I did back in the day called The Misadventures of Awkward Black Girl. You know what it is. And honestly, that's how I felt all the time, just awkward and black. And I felt like a freshman that first year. And I see all the cliques and the cool girls, and, you know, I wanted to be friends with them. And I even dealt with bullies sometimes, you guys know, as Twitter. Twitter can be so scary. Sometimes being dragged on social media feels like a low-stakes horror movie, where when you're on it, it feels like, oh, my God, and then your battery dies, and you're like, oh, I guess I'll just go outside. So now I'm in my senior year, and I feel like I learned a lot. Like, I learned how to do the, oh, my God, hey. And... That's when you see someone at a Hollywood event, and you have, like, four seconds to remember their name. So you buy a little time by starting with, oh, my God, that's you! And if they call me out on it, like, come on, Issa, you know me, I just go, excuse me. I'm Mary J. Blige, racist. But if doing my show for the last four years is like high school, then hosting SNL is my prom, and you guys are on my date.
